note: Black cottonwood (Populus trichocarpa) is treated as balsam poplar (P. balsamifera subsp. trichocarpa), the closest RSYC species in section Tacamahaca. POPU.TRE (trembling aspen) is a poorer match.

BC balsam is subalpine fir (Abies lasiocarpa), not eastern balsam fir (ABIE.BAL). The brief's ABIE.BAL suggestion was rejected because ABIE.BAL is not a BC commercial species; CASFRI maps B to ABIE_SPP.
BC code H is hemlock; western hemlock (TSUG.HET) is the dominant commercial hemlock in the province. Mountain hemlock is not separated in the source code, so this is a species-level assumption.

The brief labelled PA as paper birch, but the CASFRI crosswalk and BC VRI code set identify PA as whitebark pine (Pinus albicaulis). Paper birch is EP/BETU.PAP and is already an exact crosswalk. Whitebark pine has no RSYC target, so the area is carried in the coniferous group.
Unspecified spruce (Picea spp.) is split by ecoprovince using the same coastal/interior convention as SX.

Hybrid spruce (Picea x) has no RSYC target; coastal populations are assigned to Sitka spruce and interior/boreal populations to the white-spruce complex. This preserves the commercial spruce stream.

Yellow-cedar (Callitropsis/Chamaecyparis nootkatensis) has no RSYC species target. No other RSYC Cupressaceae is defensible at species level, so the area is carried in the coniferous model group and flagged.
